prompts.title: Executive Studio Portrait
prompts.prompt:
IDENTITY REFERENCE

Use the uploaded photo only as a face and identity reference. Preserve the subject’s recognizable identity with high fidelity: natural facial structure, skin tone, eye shape and color, nose, lips, jawline, eyebrows, ears, facial proportions, and other distinctive characteristics.

Identity takes priority over styling. Do not beautify, reshape, slim, widen, sharpen, soften, age, de-age, or reinterpret the face. Preserve natural facial asymmetry and the relative size, spacing, and placement of facial features.

If the reference shows facial hair, preserve its approximate density and grooming style; if clean-shaven, keep the subject clean-shaven. Preserve subtle identity-defining details visible in the reference. Do not invent glasses, jewelry, facial hair, tattoos, or accessories.

Do not copy the original pose, clothing, lighting, framing, or background.

SCENE

Create an ultra-realistic luxury studio executive portrait, photographed straight-on and centered. The subject should appear composed, confident, and natural, with a relaxed executive posture rather than a stiff or overly formal pose. Keep the body generally facing the camera and the face looking directly toward the lens, but allow subtle natural asymmetry in the shoulders, neck, and facial posture so the result feels human and effortless. Maintain direct eye contact and a calm, serious, confident neutral expression, with relaxed lips and no exaggerated posing.

WARDROBE

Dress the subject in a tailored cool dark charcoal-gray three-piece suit with a subtle fine woven texture, matching waistcoat, crisp white dress shirt, and a deep navy-black textured necktie.

The suit should have realistic lapels, seams, buttons, folds, stitching, and natural fabric weight. No visible logos or distracting accessories.

HAIR

Keep the hairstyle believable for the subject, with realistic density, natural hairline, individually resolved strands, subtle flyaways, and natural highlights.

BACKGROUND

Use a dark charcoal-black studio background with a subtle cool blue-teal undertone. Create a soft smoky gradient that is slightly brighter behind the head and upper shoulders and gradually falls into near-black toward the outer edges, producing gentle subject separation.

Keep the background smooth, minimal, softly out of focus, and free of scenery, objects, patterns, text, or visible studio equipment.

LIGHTING

Use refined three-point studio lighting: a large soft key light slightly above and in front of the face, gentle frontal fill to retain facial detail, and subtle rim light along the hair, ears, jawline, and shoulders.

The face should be clearly illuminated with controlled highlights on the forehead, nose, cheekbones, and lips, while retaining rich dimensional shadows. Keep the suit dark but visibly detailed, never crushed into black.

SKIN AND FACIAL DETAIL

Preserve true human skin micro-texture with natural pores and tonal variation. No plastic skin, beauty-filter smoothing, waxy texture, excessive sharpening, artificial HDR, or CGI appearance.

Both eyes must remain sharply and independently resolved with natural irises, pupils, sclera, catchlights, eyelids, tear lines, and lashes. Preserve eyebrow hairs, beard or stubble strands where applicable, lips, nostrils, ear contours, hairline, and fine facial texture.

Facial features must remain stable and anatomically coherent under close inspection, with no identity drift, altered facial proportions, mismatched eyes, warped ears, melted details, or duplicated features.

FRAMING AND COMPOSITION

Vertical 4:5 upper-torso portrait.

Frame the subject from approximately the lower chest upward, showing the full head, neck, tie, waistcoat, lapels, and both shoulders.

Keep approximately 8–10% comfortable negative space above the hair. Both shoulders should remain fully visible.

The subject must be exactly centered, with natural head-to-body proportions and no oversized head. Do not crop the hair, chin, shoulders, or tie awkwardly.

CAMERA

Professional full-frame camera look with an 85mm portrait lens at approximately f/4–f/5.6, eye-level camera position, tack-sharp focus on both eyes and facial features, realistic optical rendering, smooth tonal falloff, rich blacks, controlled contrast, natural dynamic range, and restrained cinematic color grading.

The final image should look like a genuine high-end executive studio photograph: photorealistic, sophisticated, powerful, minimal, timeless, and polished without appearing artificially retouched.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS

No smile unless naturally present in the reference, no strong head tilt, no dramatic three-quarter pose, no side profile, no crossed arms, no visible hands, no casual clothing, no colorful suit, no patterned tie, no busy background, no text, no logos, no invented eyewear or facial hair, no beauty filter, no waxy skin, no distorted face, no altered identity, no blurry facial details, no oversized head, no CGI or rendered appearance.
